title: Redesign Wendy's async message/notification queue (Gas Town mail-inspired)
description: Redesign Wendy's async inbound-message / notification handling, inspired by Gas Town's mayor mail system + stop-hook model. Current design is poll-based and ad-hoc; aim for a more elegant durable-queue solution.
design:
CURRENT STATE (reviewed in wendy_v2/mayor/rig):
- bin/msg: sends a Discord message via Wendy's internal API. Has --force to skip a 'new-message interrupt check' (i.e. msg refuses/bails if new messages arrived mid-turn unless forced).
- bin/msgs: polls/fetches new Discord messages since a watermark; flags (-n, --all, --raw); handles synthetic/context messages; Pacific-time display.
- bin/wake, bin/react: wake/notification + reactions helpers.
- Stop hooks (config/hooks/): msg_reminder.sh (parses transcript JSONL, blocks the Stop if Wendy didn't call 'msg' this turn, asking 'was that intentional?'); journal_stop_check.sh (blocks Stop if no recent journal entry); prompt_bookkeeping.sh.
Pain points to address: watermark/poll model + transcript-grep heuristics are fragile (the msg_reminder hook literally greps transcript lines for 'msg' word-boundaries; msgs relies on a watermark; msg's mid-turn interrupt check is the only concurrency guard).

WHAT TO BORROW FROM GAS TOWN MAIL:
- A durable inbox/queue with stable message IDs, read/unread state, threading, and priority (cf. gt mail inbox/read/send).
- Harness-injected notifications on turn boundaries ('you have N unread', 'remember to reply to X') instead of transcript-grepping — i.e. a UserPromptSubmit/Stop hook that reads queue STATE, not the transcript.
- Clean interrupt semantics for messages arriving mid-turn (replace msg --force new-message check with a queue-backed model).

DELIVERABLE: a design proposal (then implementation) for a queue-backed async messaging layer: durable message store, ID/threaded inbound queue, state-driven stop/prompt hooks, and a send path with sane concurrency/interrupt handling. Keep Discord as transport; this is about the queue + hook ergonomics.
acceptance_criteria: A written design replacing the watermark/transcript-grep model with a durable, ID-addressed message queue + state-driven hooks; reviewed before implementation. Covers inbound queueing, read/unread, mid-turn arrival handling, and the stop-hook reminder rebuilt on queue state rather than transcript parsing.

title: Async queue: per-message read/unread + threading + priority (deferred from wv-e4m)
description: Deferred from the async-queue refinement (hq-d5f). The current per-channel scalar seen-cursor is adequate for linear Discord channels, so per-message read/unread state, message threading, and priority were intentionally NOT built. Revisit only if a concrete need arises (e.g. multi-thread fan-out or prioritised system messages). See config/docs/async-message-queue.md section 3.5.
notes: Reviewed during hq-kj6b improvements pass (2026-06-23). NOT implemented: per-message read/unread + threading + priority remain speculative with no concrete need. config/docs/async-message-queue.md sec 3.5 states the linear per-channel cursor is sufficient for Discord's model. Implementing would be a behavior-changing, non-low-risk addition, conflicting with the hq-kj6b 'CONSERVATIVE on behavior' directive. Stays deferred; revisit only when a concrete multi-thread/priority need arises.
